steps.title: Triangles — rules to know
steps.intro: The general triangle rules. The angle sum is the one you will use most.

head: Rule
Statement
Remember
rows: vertex → midpoint of the opposite side
may fall outside an obtuse triangle
\(=\) sum of the two interior angles not next to it
the straight line is the shortest route
strict — never equal to either end

tips: Angle outside the triangle? Move it inside with vertical or adjacent angles first.
An expression of several angles? Write them all with ONE unknown — it usually cancels.

steps.intro: Isosceles means symmetric; equilateral means symmetric from every direction.

head: Triangle
Sides
Angles
Key fact

every vertex line is a symmetry line

tips: Isosceles vertex angle \(v\): each base angle is \((180°-v):2\).
Several isosceles triangles share a vertex? Find the whole angle first, then subtract the part.

steps.stem: ABC is an equilateral triangle. Point D lies on BC. Given: \(\angle DAC=30°\) and \(DC=6\) cm. What is AB (in cm)?
explanation: Angle A is 60°, so AD bisects it into two 30° angles. In an equilateral triangle the angle bisector is also a median, so BD=DC=6. Hence BC=12 and AB=12.

steps.title: Triangle area — formulas
steps.intro: Area is a side times the height to that side, over 2 — learn the equilateral formula by heart.

head: Shape
Area
Remember
rows: altitude outside? use only the side
from Pythagoras on half the triangle

tips: Triangles between parallel lines have the same height — the area ratio is the base ratio.
Subtracting equilateral areas? Keep the denominator 4 until the end.

steps.title: The Pythagorean theorem
steps.intro: Right triangles only: the squares of the legs add up to the square of the hypotenuse.

head: Looking for
Do
Formula
rows: add the squares, then take the root
hypotenuse square minus leg square, then the root

tips: Find the right-angle mark first; the hypotenuse is opposite it.
The hypotenuse is always the longest side — eliminate choices that are not longer than both legs.
A root answer is fine: \(\sqrt{65}\) is a finished length.

steps.title: Special right triangles
steps.intro: One side is enough to find the other two.

head: Triangle
Sides
Moves
rows: short leg \(\times2\) = hypotenuse · short \(\times\sqrt3\) = long · long \(\div\sqrt3\) = short
altitude = \(\frac a2\) — two golden triangles back to back · area = \(\frac{a^2\sqrt3}{4}\)

tips: Short leg is opposite \(30°\), long leg opposite \(60°\) — double only the short leg.
Dividing by a root: ignore the root, divide, attach it back — \(\frac{9}{\sqrt3}=3\sqrt3\), \(\frac{14}{\sqrt2}=7\sqrt2\).

choices: Angle A is the largest angle
explanation: The third side must exceed 26−19=7. Its full range is 7<BC<45, so BC need not be smaller than 19 or larger than 26.

steps.stem: In a right triangle, one acute angle is \(2\alpha\). What is the exterior angle adjacent to the other acute angle?
explanation: The two remote interior angles are 90° and 2α. Their sum is the requested exterior angle,90°+2α.

steps.stem: In a right triangle, one acute angle is x. The other is divided into five equal angles, each measuring x. What is x?
explanation: The two acute angles total 90°. They contain six copies of x, so 6x=90° and x=15°.

steps.stem: The exterior angles adjacent to the interior angles at P and Q of triangle PQR are u and v, respectively. Given: u>v. Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: Angle P=180°−u and angle Q=180°−v. Since u>v, angle P<angle Q. Their opposite sides satisfy QR<PR.

explanation: The symmetry line AD bisects angle A, so angle EAC=24°. Since AE=EC, angle ACE=24° too. The exterior angle x at E equals 24°+24°=48°.

steps.stem: A triangle has apex angle p and an exterior angle q at its left base vertex. A line parallel to the base intersects the extension of the right side. The angle r there corresponds to the exterior angle at the right base vertex. Which expression equals r?
explanation: The left interior angle is 180°−q. The right exterior angle equals that angle plus the apex p. Parallel lines transfer it to r, giving 180°−q+p.

steps.stem: An isosceles triangle has perimeter 38 cm. Its base is 6 cm shorter than each equal side. What is the base length (in cm)?
explanation: The side lengths are x, x, x−6. Thus 3x−6=38, giving x=44 divided by 3. The base is 26 divided by 3.

steps.stem: A triangle has two sides of lengths 9 cm and 14 cm. If the third side has an integer length, how many different lengths are possible?
explanation: The third side is strictly between 5 and 23. Its integer values are 6 through 22, which gives 22−6+1=17.

steps.stem: A triangle has area 45 cm² and a side of length 15 cm. What is the altitude to that side (in cm)?
explanation: 45=15h divided by 2. Multiply by 2 and divide by 15 to obtainh=6.

steps.stem: A right triangle has hypotenuse 29 cm and one leg 20 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Its square is 29²−20²=841−400=441, giving 21. Half of 20×21 is 210.

steps.stem: An equilateral triangle has area \(25\sqrt3\) cm². What is its perimeter (in cm)?
explanation: s²√3 divided by 4=25√3, so s²=100 and s=10. The perimeter is 3s=30.

steps.stem: A median divides a triangle into two smaller triangles. One of them has area 19 cm². What is the area of the original triangle (in cm²)?
explanation: The two triangle areas are equal because the median bisects the base and they share the same height. Add 19+19=38.

steps.stem: A right isosceles triangle has perimeter \(16+8\sqrt2\) cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: If each leg is t, the perimeter is 2t+t√2=t(2+√2). The given perimeter is 8(2+√2), so t=8. Its area is 8×8 divided by 2=32.

steps.stem: ABC is an equilateral triangle. D, A and E lie on one line, E lies on BC, and F lies on the extension of BA beyond A. Based on this information and the information in the figure, which expression equals q?
explanation: Angle B is 60°. Angle BAE is vertically opposite q, and angle AEB is 180°−p. Therefore 60°+q+180°−p=180°, giving q=p−60°.

steps.stem: Which of the following triangles is not necessarily isosceles?
choices: A triangle with a median of length 6 cm drawn to a side of length 4 cm
A triangle in which an altitude also bisects the angle at its starting vertex
A triangle in which a median is perpendicular to the side it meets
explanation: Angles 76° and 52° leave a third angle of 52°, giving equal opposite sides. An altitude that bisects its vertex angle produces congruent right triangles. A perpendicular median also produces congruent right triangles. A median with a specified length alone does not force symmetry.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, triangles ABC and ACD are right triangles. The marked lengths are in cm. What is the area of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm²)?
explanation: ABC is a 6–8–10 triangle, so AC=10. ACD has leg 10 and hypotenuse 26, so its other leg is 24. The two areas are 6×8 divided by 2=24 and 10×24 divided by 2=120. Their sum is 144.

steps.stem: Which of the following triangles is not necessarily equilateral?
choices: A triangle in which an altitude also bisects the angle at its starting vertex
A triangle with two angles of 60°
An isosceles triangle with one angle of 60°
An isosceles triangle whose base is twice half of an equal side
explanation: An altitude that also bisects its starting angle makes the triangle isosceles. It does not force the base to equal the other two sides. For example, a triangle with sides 5, 5 and 6 has this symmetry line but is not equilateral.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, ABC is a right isosceles triangle with \(AB=BC=4\) cm, and ACD is equilateral. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ABCD (in cm)?
explanation: The hypotenuse AC of the right isosceles triangle is 4√2. Both outside sides of the equilateral triangle, AD and CD, are therefore 4√2. The boundary is AB+BC+CD+DA=8+8√2. AC lies inside and is not counted.

steps.stem: In an isosceles triangle, each equal side is four times as long as the base. What is the ratio of the perimeter to the length of an equal side?
explanation: Let the base be one unit. The other sides are four units each, making a perimeter of nine units. The requested ratio is 9 to 4, or 9 divided by 4.

steps.stem: Triangles ABC and ACD are right at B and C, respectively, and have equal areas. Given: \(AB=9\) cm and \(BC=12\) cm. What is CD (in cm)?
explanation: ABC is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle, so AC=15. Its area is 9×12 divided by 2=54. In ACD the perpendicular legs are AC and CD, so 15×CD divided by 2=54 and CD=36 divided by 5.

steps.stem: At each vertex of a triangle, consider the reflex angle consisting of the full turn outside its interior angle. What is the average of these three reflex angles?
explanation: The three full turns total 1080°. Removing the three interior angles removes 180°, leaving 900°. The average is 900° divided by 3=300°.

steps.stem: The shortest and longest sides of a triangle are 2 cm and 7 cm, respectively. Which of the following could be the length of its third side (in cm)?
explanation: The third side x must satisfy 2+x>7, so x>5. It must also be shorter than the longest side, 7. Of the choices, only 6.5 lies between 5 and 7.

steps.stem: In triangle ABC, \(AB=AC\). BD bisects angle B and meets AC at D. Given: \(AD=DB\). What is angle B?
explanation: Let each half of angle B be x. Since AD=DB, angle BAD also equals x. The base angles B and C are equal, so the triangle angles are x, 2x and 2x. Thus 5x=180°, giving x=36° and angle B=72°.

steps.stem: AD is an altitude in triangle ABC, with D on BC. Given: \(BD=\frac34BC\). The area of ADC is 14 cm². What is the area of ABD (in cm²)?
explanation: BD is three quarters of BC, leaving one quarter for DC. The ratio BD:DC is 3:1. Both triangles have altitude AD, so their areas are in that same ratio. Hence ABD has area 3×14=42.

steps.stem: In triangle ABC, angle B is 35° and angle A is greater than 45°. BC is extended beyond C to D. Which of the following cannot be the measure of angle ACD?
explanation: Angle ACD equals angle A plus angle B. It is therefore greater than 45°+35°=80°. The value 75° is impossible. Each other choice is below 180° and gives a valid angle A greater than 45°.

steps.stem: Triangle ABC is right at C, with \(AC=12\) cm and \(BC=16\) cm. D is the midpoint of BC. Which statement compares triangles ADC and ADB correctly?
choices: Their areas are equal, and ADC has the smaller perimeter
Their areas and perimeters are equal
ADC has the smaller area and the smaller perimeter
Their areas are equal, and ADB has the smaller perimeter
explanation: DC=DB, and both triangles have the same altitude from A. Their areas are therefore equal. Their perimeters share AD and equal base pieces, so only AC and AB differ. The hypotenuse AB is longer than leg AC, making ADC’s perimeter smaller.

steps.stem: The angles of a triangle are \(2x\), \(4x\) and \(6x\). Which of the following could be its side lengths (in cm)?
explanation: The angles total 12x=180°, so x=15°. The actual angles are 30°,60° and 90°, whose opposite sides are in the ratio 1:√3:2. Only 5,5√3,10 has that ratio.

steps.stem: A, E and B lie on one line in that order; D, E and C lie on another. The marked angles at A and C are right angles. Given: \(BC=2\), \(CE=2\sqrt3\) and \(AD=4\sqrt3\). What is AB?
explanation: In EBC, the legs 2 and 2√3 give hypotenuse EB=4 and angle BEC=30°. Its vertically opposite angle AED is also 30°. In AED, AD=4√3 is opposite 30°, so AE=4√3×√3=12. Thus AB=12+4=16.

explanation: The left right triangle is a 5–12–13 triangle, so AD=5. In ADC, DC²=61−25=36, so DC=6. The whole base is BD+DC=12+6=18.

steps.stem: Which of the following is necessarily true for every isosceles triangle?
choices: Each equal side is longer than the base
Every altitude is also an angle bisector
The altitude to the base is shorter than an equal side
explanation: The altitude to the base forms two right triangles. In either one, an equal side is the hypotenuse and the altitude is a leg. The hypotenuse is longer, so the stated comparison must hold.

steps.stem: A, C and B lie on one line. CE bisects angle ACD, and CF bisects angle DCB. E and F lie on these bisectors. Given: angle CEF is \(2t\). Which expression equals angle EFC?
explanation: Angles ACD and DCB total 180°. Their halves total 90°, so angle ECF is a right angle. The other two angles in ECF must total 90°. Since one is 2t, the other is 90°−2t.

steps.stem: Two angles of a triangle are α and β. At the third vertex, the reflex angle outside the triangle is divided into three equal angles, each measuring δ. Which expression equals δ?
explanation: The third interior angle is 180°−α−β. Its outside reflex angle is 360°−(180°−α−β)=180°+α+β. Divide this by 3 to get 60°+(α+β) divided by 3.

steps.stem: ABC is right at A, with \(AB=8\) cm and \(AC=15\) cm. AD is the altitude to BC. What is AD (in cm)?
explanation: The hypotenuse is 17. Using the legs, the area is 8×15 divided by 2=60. Using BC and AD, it is 17×AD divided by 2. Equating them gives AD=120 divided by 17.

steps.stem: The side opposite an obtuse angle of a triangle is 8 cm long. Which of the following could be the sum of the other two side lengths (in cm)?
explanation: The two other sides must total more than 8 by the triangle inequality. Each is shorter than 8 because it lies opposite a smaller angle, so their sum is less than 16. Only 10 remains. It is attainable: sides 5,5,8 form a triangle, and 8²>5²+5² makes the angle opposite 8 obtuse.

steps.stem: One triangle has angles \(2p\), \(q\) and 42°. Another has angles \(p\), \(2q\) and 66°. What is \(p+q\)?
explanation: The angle sums give 2p+q=138° and p+2q=114°. Adding gives 3(p+q)=252°, so p+q=84°. This matches the requested sum directly.

steps.stem: In the accompanying figure, \(AC=BC\), \(AB\parallel CD\), and AD bisects angle BAC. Given: angle ACB is \(2t\). Which expression equals x?
explanation: The two equal base angles are each (180°−2t) divided by 2=90°−t. AD halves the angle at A, so angle BAD=45°−t divided by 2. Alternate angles between the parallel lines give x=angle BAD.

steps.stem: A right triangle has perimeter 60 cm and hypotenuse 26 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: Let the legs be a and b. Their sum is 60−26=34, while a²+b²=26²=676. From (a+b)²=a²+b²+2 ab, we get 1156=676+2 ab, so ab=240. The area is ab divided by 2=120.

steps.stem: An equilateral triangle and a right isosceles triangle have equal perimeters. Each side of the equilateral triangle is 8 cm. What is a leg of the right isosceles triangle (in cm)?
explanation: The common perimeter is 24. If a leg is x, the hypotenuse is x√2, giving x(2+√2)=24. Multiply numerator and denominator of 24 divided by (2+√2) by (2−√2). The denominator becomes 2, leaving 12(2−√2).

steps.stem: In triangle ABC, D lies on BC and \(BD:DC=2:5\). E is the midpoint of AD. What is the ratio of the area of EBD to the area of ABC?
explanation: Triangle ABD has two sevenths of the whole area because BD is two sevenths of BC. E is halfway from D to A, so its perpendicular height above BC is half of A’s. Thus EBD has half of two sevenths, or one seventh, of the whole area.

steps.stem: A triangle has integer side lengths. Two sides are 6 cm and 10 cm. How many possible third-side lengths make the 10 cm side the unique longest side?
explanation: The triangle inequality gives 4<x<16. Requiring 10 to be the unique longest side adds x<10. The integer possibilities are 5,6,7,8 and 9: five values.

steps.stem: A triangle has side lengths 10 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
explanation: The altitude bisects the 12 cm base into two 6 cm pieces. Each half is a6–8–10 right triangle, so the altitude is 8. The area is 12×8 divided by 2=48.

steps.stem: In a 30°–60°–90° triangle, the difference between the hypotenuse and the shorter leg is 7 cm. What is the area (in cm²)?
explanation: The side ratio is 1:√3:2. If the short leg is s, the difference between hypotenuse 2s and short leg s is s itself. Thus s=7 and the other leg is 7√3. Half their product is 49√3 divided by 2.

steps.stem: Two triangles share a base of length 14 cm. Their third vertices lie on opposite sides of the base line, at perpendicular distances of 5 cm and 9 cm from it. What is the area of the figure formed by their union (in cm²)?
explanation: The triangles lie on opposite sides of their common base and do not overlap in area. Their areas are 14×5 divided by 2=35 and 14×9 divided by 2=63. Together they cover 98 cm².
